the SWEN trial was a randomized, controlled trial to assess the impact of extended nevirapine (NVP) prophylaxis on HIV transmission in infants born to HIV-infected women in Pune, India (NCT0006132).

we found that the growth of HIV-exposed and HIV-infected infants in India is poor and that the timing of HIV infection and the use of nevirapine to prevent mother-to-child transmission have significant impact on growth outcomes.
we found that growth indices were similar among HIV-infected and exposed uninfected infants in India, but that growth indices diverged rapidly and significantly in the HIV-infected group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early growth monitoring of all infants born to mothers with HIV is an important low cost strategy for improving health outcomes of these infants in resource limited settings.
early growth faltering is a common occurrence in both HIV-infexed and exposed infants in this resource-limited setting and that this is a critical time to intervene.
